chapter: Freelancing, Miller and the girls' bands
title: Why the girls' band drew crowds and the Paramount opening
summary: The band was favored for being women, opened at the Paramount, previewed in Rochester, and Hutton wanted it to swing like Basie.

bands.name: Ina Ray Hutton and Her Orchestra

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, now, when you say they were very popular, was it because they were girls or was it because they were --
Well, they favored them because they was girls.
But in the end, they were playing more than they thought they were going to play. They played at the -- they come out of rehearsal with the second band. I went

and got a new band. And they come out with the second band, and they opened in the Paramount Theatre in Newark. And Lola Lane was on the program, MGM was there, Mitchell Lewis and I and when they closed that theatre, after opening over here for two days, then they said, well, they could open at the Paramount in New York.
So I didn't like that. I said, they must be favoring the girls. There ain't no bands can go open out of rehearsal with a new band and go to the Paramount in New York.

I say -- but they could play. But you still needed a reputation behind you. Basie hadn't even got any -- and we opened up in Rochester, in a preview, and Duke came up, had Duke to come up and a few other guys, to see what they thought about the band.

And some of the guys said, well, I don't like the girls, they're playing too much like boys, because they had them fanning hats, and they said, that don't look nice. And they wanted pretty girls like a melody, like this. Ina Hutton didn't like this, see, I want to swing like Basie, so the band got so they could swing. They had good musicians, of course, We had this Alice Wills on trombone, who travelled (inaudible). And she played 26 instruments perfectly. Played 26 different instruments. And she was a blond, looked good, and she played (inaudible) and they traveled around together.
Got a girl out of a conservatory out of Zanesville, Ohio, played a piano. They could really play, see. So you had to have (inaudible) band but you got to know your limitations.
Yeah. You didn't conduct on stage or anything.

No, if I did, it would be from the wings sometimes, getting out of something, and she (inaudible). Nobody could see me because they didn't know -- but sometimes I'd have to start a number off, or get it started. And she'd make an entrance.
But she was hard to handle, and -- everybody favored her, though, guys like the Marx Brothers and all those guys. She hung around with all them guys. It was a big time band.
